title: Last One Standing in the Circle
statement:
n players stand in a circle, numbered 1 to n clockwise. Starting with player 1, count k players clockwise, including the player you start on. The player you land on leaves the circle. The next count starts at the player just clockwise of the one who left.

Repeat until one player remains, and return that player's number.

examples.why: Counting 1, 2 removes player 2. From 3: 3, 4 removes 4. From 1: 1, 3 removes 3. Player 1 is left.
With k = 1 every count ends where it starts, so players leave in order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Players leave in the order 3, 1, 5, 2. The count wraps past the end of the circle each time it runs out of players.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 100000 : r.int(1, 12); return [n, big ? r.int(n >> 1, n) : r.int(1, n)]; }
hints: Simulating with an array works: the next player to leave is at index (current + k − 1) mod size. What does each removal cost?
After the first player leaves, the rest is the same game with n − 1 players, just with everyone renumbered so the next count starts at position 0.
If w(m) is the winner's 0-based position in a game of m players, then w(m) = (w(m − 1) + k) mod m, with w(1) = 0. Build it up from 1 to n.

explain.intuition:
Simulation is honest but slow: removing from the middle of an array shifts everything after it, so the whole game costs O(n²).

The trick is to notice the game repeats itself. Use 0-based positions. In a game of m players, the first one to leave is at position k − 1, and the next count starts at position k. Now relabel the m − 1 survivors starting from there: you have a fresh game of m − 1 players. If its winner is at w in the new labels, it was at (w + k) mod m in the old ones. Start from 1 player (winner at 0) and grow to n; add 1 at the end to return to 1-based numbers.
steps: Set w = 0: with one player, position 0 wins.
For m from 2 to n, set w = (w + k) mod m.
pitfalls: Counting k steps from the player you start on instead of including them. That removes the wrong player every round.
Starting the next count at the removed player's old index plus one. After removing from an array, the next player already sits at the removed index.
Forgetting the final + 1 and returning a 0-based position.

solutions.title: Simulate with an array
solutions.idea: Keep the players in an array. The next player to leave is (start + k − 1) mod size; remove it and continue from the same index.

solutions.title: Grow the game one player at a time
solutions.idea: The winner of m players sits k places after the winner of m − 1 players, wrapped around m.

followups: Return the full order in which players leave, faster than O(n²). (Hint: a Fenwick tree to find the j-th remaining player.)
For k = 2 there is a closed form in terms of the highest power of two below n. Can you derive it?
